content.text:
This is conclusive: commit `8215a398219ae55ae3568a7a3946627dd3493e70` originally introduced *all* of the `isDistinctFrom` implementations for the scalar types (Bigint, Boolean, Char, Color, Date, Double, Integer, IntervalDayTime, IntervalYearMonth, IpAddress, Real, Smallint, Time, TimeWithTimeZone, Timestamp, TimestampWithTimeZone, Tinyint, Unknown, Varbinary, Varchar, Json) as well as the structural-type operators `ArrayDistinctFromOperator`, `MapDistinctFromOperator`, and `RowDistinctFromOperator`, all exclusively using the `NULL_FLAG` invocation convention that requires extracting/boxing each value out of the `Block` via `readNativeValue`/`defaultValue`. This is exactly the inefficient pattern that HEAD's commit (f09c02aa83) explicitly targets and eliminates by adding a second `BLOCK_POSITION`-convention implementation "so that... it's no longer necessary to extract the value out of the Block."

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 8215a398219ae55ae3568a7a3946627dd3493e70

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation approach:** The fixing commit (f09c02aa83) touches essentially every `isDistinctFrom` scalar operator plus `ArrayDistinctFromOperator`, `MapDistinctFromOperator`, `RowDistinctFromOperator`, and `JsonOperators`, in every case adding a *second* implementation using the `BLOCK_POSITION` invocation convention alongside the pre-existing `NULL_FLAG` implementation. Its message explicitly states the goal: avoid "extract[ing] the value out of the Block" for performance. That phrasing points directly at the pre-existing implementation pattern as the root cause, so I traced the git history of the affected files (`ArrayDistinctFromOperator.java`, `BigintOperators.java`, etc.) to find when the `NULL_FLAG`-only `isDistinctFrom` methods were first introduced.

**(2) The specific change:** Commit `8215a39821` ("Reimplement IS DISTINCT FROM as an operator") is the commit that originally created every one of these `isDistinctFrom` operator methods (confirmed via `git show` — new files for `ArrayDistinctFromOperator.java`, `MapDistinctFromOperator.java`, `RowDistinctFromOperator.java`, and new methods added to `BigintOperators.java`, `BooleanOperators.java`, etc.). Critically, it implemented `ArrayDistinctFromOperator`/`MapDistinctFromOperator`/`RowDistinctFromOperator` by iterating elements and calling `TypeUtils.readNativeValue(...)` plus `Defaults.defaultValue(...)` to box every element value out of the `Block`, then invoking the element's `isDistinctFrom` MethodHandle via the `NULL_FLAG` convention. Because only the `NULL_FLAG` convention existed, there was no way to compare block positions directly — forcing this costly extraction on every element of every array/map/row comparison. This is precisely the inefficient code path f09c02aa83's diff shows being removed/augmented (e.g., the removed `readNativeValue`/`defaultValue` calls in `ArrayDistinctFromOperator.java`).

**(3) Supporting evidence:** `git show 8215a39821 -- ArrayDistinctFromOperator.java` (and the Map/Row equivalents) produces code byte-for-byte matching the "before" side of the diff in f09c02aa83 (same `readNativeValue`/`defaultValue`/`NULL_FLAG` pattern). Likewise, `git show 8215a39821 -- BigintOperators.java` shows the exact `isDistinctFrom(long, boolean, long, boolean)` method with `NULL_FLAG`-only convention that f09c02aa83 later wraps in a nested class and supplements with a `BLOCK_POSITION` variant. No intervening commit altered this fundamental convention choice for these operators.

**Uncertainty:** f09c02aa83 is framed as a performance fix ("expected to resolve performance issue"), not a correctness bug fix — there is no clear functional/correctness regression being corrected for the common types. If the study's definition of "bug" is strictly a correctness defect rather than a performance defect, then 8215a398 is still the most defensible answer since it is the sole origin of the exact pattern the fixing commit removes; there is no other commit in the history that independently introduced this NULL_FLAG-based value-extraction approach. I did not find evidence of a distinct, later-introduced correctness bug that this specific commit resolves (aside from an unrelated pre-existing bug in `DecimalInequalityOperators.distinctBlockPositionLongLong`, which is not modified by this commit and is not what this fix addresses).
